title.es: Proyecto de escritura: edición de precisión

es: Editar un borrador con precisión: corregir tiempos, registro, cohesión, conectores y concisión eligiendo el cambio mínimo.

teaching.en: We edit in layers: first the meaning, then the cohesion, then the wording.
teaching.es: Editamos por capas: primero el significado, luego la cohesión y después la redacción.
teaching.explanationEs: Revisar todo a la vez hace perder errores; cada capa tiene su pregunta.
segments: We edit in layers: first the meaning,
then the cohesion, then the wording.
teaching.audioText: We edit in layers: first the meaning, then the cohesion, then the wording.

teaching.en: A connector must match the logic: We lowered the price; as a result, sales rose.
teaching.es: Un conector debe respetar la lógica: Bajamos el precio; como resultado, las ventas subieron.
teaching.explanationEs: Suma (moreover), contrasta (however) o da resultado (as a result): elige según la relación real.
segments: A connector must match the logic: We lowered
the price; as a result, sales rose.
teaching.audioText: A connector must match the logic: We lowered the price; as a result, sales rose.

teaching.en: A wordy sentence hides its point: In order to finish, we need time becomes To finish, we need time.
teaching.es: Una frase prolija esconde su idea: In order to finish, we need time pasa a To finish, we need time.
teaching.explanationEs: Si puedes quitar palabras sin perder significado, la frase estaba inflada.
segments: A wordy sentence hides its point: In order to finish,
we need time becomes To finish, we need time.
teaching.audioText: A wordy sentence hides its point: In order to finish, we need time becomes To finish, we need time.

teaching.en: Good writers tighten a sentence by cutting repetition: the newly opened shop, not the new, recently opened shop.
teaching.es: Quien escribe bien ajusta una frase eliminando repeticiones: the newly opened shop, no the new, recently opened shop.
teaching.explanationEs: New y recently opened dicen lo mismo: un solo adverbio basta.
segments: Good writers tighten a sentence by cutting repetition: the
newly opened shop, not the new, recently opened shop.
teaching.audioText: Good writers tighten a sentence by cutting repetition: the newly opened shop, not the new, recently opened shop.

teaching.en: Keep the tense steady: When the manager arrived, the team had already finished.
teaching.es: Mantén estable el tiempo verbal: Cuando llegó el jefe, el equipo ya había terminado.
teaching.explanationEs: Lo anterior a otro hecho pasado lleva had + participio; no mezcles tiempos sin motivo.
segments: Keep the tense steady: When the manager
arrived, the team had already finished.
teaching.audioText: Keep the tense steady: When the manager arrived, the team had already finished.

teaching.en: A vague phrase such as a lot of weakens a report; a large number of is more exact.
teaching.es: Una expresión vaga como a lot of debilita un informe; a large number of es más exacta.
teaching.explanationEs: El registro académico y profesional prefiere cantidades o expresiones precisas.
segments: A vague phrase such as a lot of weakens
a report; a large number of is more exact.
teaching.audioText: A vague phrase such as a lot of weakens a report; a large number of is more exact.

prompt.es: Marca 1: elige el conector que respeta la lógica.

feedback.es: Terminar pronto es la consecuencia del esfuerzo; however y on the other hand marcan contraste.

hint.es: El segundo hecho es la consecuencia del primero.

origin.text: The team worked hard all week; ___, they finished the report early.

prompt.es: Completa: «A pesar de la lluvia, terminamos la encuesta.»

feedback.es: Despite se une directamente al nombre, con su determinante y sin of: despite the rain.

hint.es: Despite va seguido del nombre; este necesita su determinante.

origin.text: Despite ___ rain, we finished the survey.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Además de la encuesta, realizamos entrevistas.»

answer.text: In addition to the survey, we held interviews

feedback.es: In addition to + nombre añade información y abre la frase, seguido de coma.

hint.es: Empieza por la expresión que añade información.

prompt.es: Marca 4: ¿qué versión es más concisa y precisa?

choices.text: The match was postponed because of the fact that there was rain.
Since the rain had fallen, the match was postponed.
Because it rained, the match was postponed.

feedback.es: Because dice lo mismo que due to the fact that con menos palabras y sin cambiar el sentido.

origin.text: Due to the fact that it rained, the match was postponed.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace la editora con la frase del borrador.

choices.text: She replaces a vague phrase with an exact one.
She adds a connector of contrast.
She moves the sentence to the end.

feedback.es: La editora cambia a lot of por una cifra: un registro profesional exige expresiones precisas.

origin.audio: The draft said: We did a lot of interviews. The editor changed it to: We carried out forty interviews. She explained that a lot of is vague, while forty is exact.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada conector con la relación lógica que expresa.

feedback.es: Elegir bien el conector depende de la lógica: suma, contraste, resultado o ejemplo.

prompt.es: Marca 9: corrige el conector para expresar un resultado.

answer.text: The prices were lower; consequently, sales rose.
accepted: The prices were lower; consequently, sales rose.
The prices were lower; therefore, sales rose.
The prices were lower, so sales rose.
The prices were lower; as a result, sales rose.
The prices were lower; thus, sales rose.
The prices were lower; hence, sales rose.
The prices were lower; for this reason, sales rose.

feedback.es: Las ventas suben a causa de los precios bajos: hace falta un conector de resultado, no de contraste.

origin.text: The prices were lower; however, sales rose.

prompt.es: Completa: «Le agradeceríamos que enviara el informe para el lunes.»

feedback.es: En un registro formal, la petición se suaviza con if you could + verbo base.

origin.text: We would be grateful if you ___ send the report by Monday.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué corrige la editora en el borrador.

choices.text: She replaces the verb with a more formal word.
She adds a form that shows which event came first.

feedback.es: Había terminado ocurrió antes de la llegada: had finished ordena los dos hechos pasados.

origin.audio: The draft said: When the director arrived, we already finished the report. The editor says the verb should be had finished, because the report was completed before the director came.

prompt.es: Marca 12: ¿a qué se refiere «Such a habit»?

feedback.es: Such a habit retoma la costumbre descrita en la primera frase: usar el móvil en clase.

origin.text: Many students use phones in class. This leads to distraction. Such a habit can be reduced with clear rules.

prompt.es: Marca 6: quita la repetición sin perder información.

choices.text: The newly opened shop is very popular.
The new and recently opened shop is very popular.

feedback.es: Newly opened resume new y recently opened; quitar ambos borraría información y mantenerlos repite la idea.

origin.text: The new, recently opened shop is very popular.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Editamos primero el significado y después la redacción.»

answer.text: We edit the meaning first and then the wording
accepted: We edit the meaning first and then the wording
First we edit the meaning and then the wording
We first edit the meaning and then the wording

feedback.es: Las capas de la revisión se ordenan con first y then: primero el sentido, después la forma.

prompt.es: Marca 11: sustituye la frase coloquial por una de registro neutro.

answer.text: The manager was annoyed because the report was late.
accepted: The manager was annoyed because the report was late.
The director was upset because the report was late.
The manager was displeased because the report was late.
The boss was annoyed because the report was delayed.

feedback.es: En un informe se evita got really mad: un adjetivo neutro (annoyed, upset) mantiene el sentido con más formalidad.

origin.text: The boss got really mad because the report was late.

evidenceGroups: because the report was submitted late
